ripenessTips.description: Brown hairy skin, similar to taro. No soft spots.

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Very firm and heavy.

funFact: Malanga is a staple root in Cuban and Caribbean cuisine, often used in soups and fried into chips.
storageTip: Store in a cool, dry place for up to 2 weeks. Must be cooked before eating.

name: Boniato

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: Red-purple skin with white flesh. No cracks or sprouts.

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Firm and heavy. Avoid soft spots.

funFact: Boniato (white sweet potato) is drier and fluffier than orange sweet potatoes, making it popular in Latin American and Asian cuisines.
storageTip: Do not refrigerate. Store in cool, dry place for 1-2 weeks. More perishable than regular sweet potatoes.

name: Sapodilla

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Gives to gentle pressure when ripe, like a kiwi.

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: Sandy brown skin, slightly rough.

funFact: Sapodilla trees produce chicle, the original base for chewing gum. The Aztecs and Mayans chewed chicle centuries ago.
storageTip: Ripen at room temperature. Refrigerate ripe fruit for 2-3 days.

name: Chile de Arbol

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: Bright red and slim. Dried ones should be unbroken.

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Firm when fresh, crisp when dried.

funFact: Chile de arbol means 'tree chile' because the plant grows tall and woody like a small tree.
storageTip: Fresh: refrigerate for 1-2 weeks. Dried: store in airtight container for 6+ months.

name: Guaje

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: Flat pods with visible seeds. Red or green varieties.

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Pods should be firm with plump seeds inside.

funFact: Guaje seeds (huaxes) have been eaten in Mexico since pre-Columbian times and Oaxaca is named after the Nahuatl word for guaje.
storageTip: Refrigerate in pods for up to a week. Shelled seeds freeze well.

name: Verdolaga (Purslane)

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: Thick, succulent, jade-green leaves and reddish stems.

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Crisp and juicy, not wilted.

funFact: Purslane has the highest omega-3 fatty acid content of any leafy green and is the most widely distributed weed on earth.
storageTip: Refrigerate wrapped in damp paper towel for 3-4 days. Very perishable.

name: Huauzontle

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: Bright green flower clusters on thin stalks.

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Tender stems that snap easily.

funFact: Huauzontle was a sacred food of the Aztecs, often used as tribute. It is typically battered and fried with cheese.
storageTip: Very perishable. Use within 2-3 days. Refrigerate in a damp towel.

name: Xoconostle

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: Pink-purple skin with acidic green flesh. Firmer than sweet tuna.

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Firm, not soft like sweet prickly pear.

funFact: Xoconostle is the sour cousin of the prickly pear and is used in mole de olla and salsas throughout central Mexico.
storageTip: Refrigerate for up to 3 weeks — much longer-lasting than sweet tuna.

name: Quelites

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: Bright green tender leaves and shoots. Various species.

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: Tender and crisp, similar to spinach.

funFact: Quelites is a catch-all term for dozens of edible wild greens in Mexican cuisine, eaten since pre-Hispanic times.
storageTip: Very perishable. Refrigerate wrapped in damp towel and use within 2-3 days.

name: Walnut

ripenessTips.title: Feel
ripenessTips.description: In-shell: heavy for size, no rattling. Shelled: plump and not shriveled.

ripenessTips.title: Look
ripenessTips.description: No cracks or holes in the shell.

funFact: Fresh green walnuts (nuez de castilla) are essential for chiles en nogada, Mexico's patriotic dish served every September.
storageTip: In-shell: cool dry place for 3 months. Shelled: refrigerate for 6 months or freeze for a year.
